# PSY Lokalpsykiatri (Sønderborg)

PSY Lokalpsykiatri (Sønderborg) is a local psychiatric unit reported in the Danish ADHD quality database (ADHD_2024.pdf), which tracks treatment indicators for both child/adolescent and adult ADHD patients. The unit appears in the database's detailed department-level breakdowns for two separate quality indicators covering behind-the-scenes clinical practice in adult ADHD care.

Its most notable result concerns Indicator 10, which measures the share of adult treatment courses in which a patient's social support needs were assessed within 120 days of starting treatment. This was the first year this indicator was reported nationally, and results showed significant shortfalls against the 90% quality target both nationally (37%) and regionally (14–52%)[^src1]. Against this backdrop, PSY Lokalpsykiatri (Sønderborg) recorded only 37 out of 136 relevant treatment courses meeting the standard, a fulfillment rate of 27% (with a confidence interval of 20–35%) — placing it below the national average and far under the 90% development goal[^src1]. This shortfall is the basis of the entity's documented significance: the unit's 27% score is explicitly noted as "betydeligt under udviklingsmålet på 90 %" (significantly below the 90% development target).

The steering group behind the ADHD database discussed possible reasons for the low fulfillment rates nationally, including registration practices and the data foundation drawn from child and adolescent psychiatric outpatient clinics and private hospitals, and decided to work on improving registration practice going forward[^src1].

By contrast, on Indicator 11 — which measures the share of adult treatment courses where the patient is receiving ADHD medication within 120 days of starting a care pathway — PSY Lokalpsykiatri (Sønderborg) performed considerably better, with 93 out of 136 treatment courses meeting the standard, a rate of 68% (confidence interval 60–76%)[^src2]. This indicator was also being measured for adults for the first time in 2024, following the ADHD database's expansion that year to include adult patients[^src2]. Nationally, this indicator showed wide regional variation, with Region Nordjylland reaching 85% and Region Hovedstaden only 37%, a gap the source material attributes probably to registration difficulties rather than real clinical differences[^src2].
